prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the near couch and the camera wearer’s legs/feet about 0.3–1.2 m away, the coffee table and rug about 1–2 m ahead, and the seated person and rear couch roughly 3–5 m away; the back wall, television, and doorway are farther still. Across the five frames, the viewpoint rotates and tilts rightward and downward, making the near couch sweep from the left foreground toward the centre/right while the wearer’s feet enter the lower-right foreground; the seated person shifts leftward and eventually leaves view. It clarifies depth ordering and occlusion: the table lies in front of the seated person, the near couch partly blocks the floor, and foreground legs obscure parts of the final frames. Metric distances remain approximate because monocular brightness is only a relative-depth cue, and boundaries around furniture, feet, and dark background regions appear smoothed or inconsistent.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks separate a near couch along the left foreground in frames 1–3, a chair and seated person about 3–5 m ahead, and smaller table objects—including books, a cup, bottle, remote, and television—at differing image heights and lateral positions. As the camera turns right, the coffee/dining table and its book occupy more of the central view, the near couch shifts toward the centre, and the wearer’s body appears at the bottom/right while the distant person moves out of frame; several floor objects remain roughly 1–2 m ahead. The map makes overlapping instances and partial visibility clearer, including the person against the chair, tabletop objects above the table surface, and bodies or furniture clipped by frame edges. It is unreliable in places: furniture classes change between frames, the rug/table/couch receive oversized or implausible masks, parts of the camera wearer are labelled as separate people, and small-object masks flicker or disappear.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects one body skeleton only near the centre-left of the second frame, corresponding to the seated person roughly 3–5 m in front of the camera wearer; the compact joint layout indicates a seated, bent-limb configuration with the torso approximately facing the camera. No reliable body or hand skeleton is shown for the camera wearer, despite feet and a hand becoming visible at close range in the RGB, and no pose remains as the seated person shifts out of view during the rightward camera turn. Where present, the skeleton makes joint locations and relative limb positions easier to distinguish than in the dark, partially occluded RGB view. The map is highly incomplete: it provides no usable orientation or gaze estimate across most frames, cannot establish arm’s reach, and misses partially visible or foreground body parts.
